diagnosis.headline: The payment container exited (exit 137, not OOM) at 08:40:33. Checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls now fail with DNS and no-route errors, so every checkout fails and email stops getting calls.

root_causes.cause: The payment container exited at 2026-10-24T08:40:33 with exit code 137, oom_killed=false and restart_count 0, and it has not come back. Exit 137 without an OOM kill points to a SIGKILL (for example docker stop/kill), not memory exhaustion. Because the container is gone, Docker DNS cannot resolve 'payment' and the old IP has no route to host. Checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge calls fail as a result.

affected_services.impact: Container exited at 08:40:33 and serves no requests: it has no spans and its rps is 0.
Every checkout fails (error_rate 1.0) because the Charge call to payment cannot connect. Users cannot place orders.
Gets no traffic, because checkout fails at the payment step before it would send the confirmation email.

ruled_out.reason: Memory is at 93.99% of its limit, but the container is running and healthy and frontend is not flagged in service health. The checkout failures come from the payment call, not from frontend.
The container is healthy. It is silent only because checkout fails before it would call email.
The container is running and healthy. Its errors all come from the Charge call to payment, so they are propagated, not generated inside checkout.

open_questions: What sent SIGKILL to payment (exit 137, oom_killed=false)? Check the Docker daemon events and operator actions around 08:40:33.
An earlier run (04:09) also proposed restarting payment. Is this a recurring stop, and what is behind it?
frontend memory is at 93.99% of its limit. Keep watching it for a possible leak, separate from this incident.
prevention: Set restart: unless-stopped/on-failure for payment in docker compose, and alert on container exit for critical services.
Audit who can run docker stop/kill on production containers, and require change records for them.
Make checkout fail fast with clear errors and add a circuit breaker on the payment dependency.

proposed_action.reason: The payment container is stopped (exited 137, not OOM). Starting it brings back the DNS record and endpoint that checkout's Charge calls need.
proposed_action.risk_assessment: Low. payment is stateless and currently down anyway, so restarting it cannot make things worse. If something external stopped it on purpose, it may be stopped again; check who issued the stop.
proposed_action.expected_outcome: payment spans return at about 0.057 rps, checkout error_rate drops from 1.0 to about 0, and email traffic recovers to about 0.057 rps.

objections.text: The ruled-out entry for checkout says its container is 'running and healthy', but no registered evidence shows checkout's container state. E7 and E8 only show the failing client span. The conclusion still holds, because the errors are DNS and no-route errors to payment, but the cited evidence doesn't support the 'healthy container' claim.

The ruled-out entry for email says 'the container is healthy', but E4 is about the payment container, and E3 only shows email has no traffic. Nothing shows email's container state. Even so, silence downstream of a failing checkout is consistent with what the evidence shows.

E9 (load-generator POST to frontend-proxy with no server span) uses the same example trace ID as E7, and E7's chain is just 'load-generator'. In some traces, then, the propagation path is unclear, and a minor frontend-proxy or ingress problem isn't fully ruled out. It is only 1 of 6 traces, though, and E8 shows the full chain ending at payment.

The cause of the SIGKILL can't be determined from this evidence. Exit 137 with oom_killed=false (E4) and no warn+ logs (E12) fit an external stop or kill, but nothing explains why it happened. The headline timestamp of 08:40:33 is also a bit off from 'stopped 189s ago' (E4). Neither point changes the origin.
